messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER: [P1] region=us-east runtime: queue depth spike detected (queue>95% for 12m), p99 token latency = 4.8s, error rate=0.8%. Alerting on-call.

sam: ack, jumping in. Looking at pool metrics and inflight distribution now.

sam: quick summary: embed-heavy customer flows are saturating low-priority slices in us-east-3. Pool inflight ~384/400 and growing -> requests queueing. High preemptible occupancy.

emily: can we prioritize premium traffic first? we should avoid impacting SLA customers.

raj: suggestion: enable priority-lane shedding (fast-path for premium), reduce max_inflight for low-priority slice, and tighten timeouts for any long-running requests. Also consider temporary quota reductions for free tier.

sam: agreed. Proposed mitigation steps (short-lived):
1) flip 'priority_lane' feature flag ON (routes premium to fast lane)
2) set low-priority slice max_inflight 400 -> 250
3) set eviction_policy -> aggressive and timeout 20s -> 15s for that slice
4) reduce free-tier per-tenant rps from 10 -> 4
5) enable fallback model routing for heavy generator customers (non-blocking, smaller model)
6) notify support + customers impacted list

emily: +1. order looks good. do we need an A/B or can we push directly?

sam: push directly, but we'll do a small canary on us-east-3 nodes first (10% traffic). watching telemetry for 3m.

sam: executing canary now.

sam: ```
# enable priority lane flag
curl -s -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/v1/flags -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"flag":"priority_lane","env":"prod","value":true}'

# patch slice config (canary)
PATCH /v1/pools/us-east-3/slices/low-priority
{
  "max_inflight": 250,
  "eviction_policy": "aggressive",
  "request_timeout_ms": 15000
}

# quota update for free tier
PATCH /v1/quotas/free-tier
{ "rps": 4 }
```

emily: saw the flag flip. canary at 10% started. metrics?

sam: early signal: queue depth down 30% on canary nodes, p99 latency down ~1.1s for premium traffic. low-tier still queued but within expected. error rate stable.

raj: good. what's customer impact? any paying customers showing errors/timeouts?

taylor: checking list: ACME-Billing (tier=standard), shoply-ci (free), internal-qa (free). ACME has 2 error spikes -> contacting support.

support-bot: Drafting customer note for ACME: "We're investigating intermittent latency for API calls in us-east. We've activated a priority routing change to reduce impact and may temporarily reduce free-tier throughput. We'll update in 30 min." Approve?

emily: approve the ACME note. add estimated resolution window: ~30-60m.

support-bot: sending now.

sam: canary looks healthy, scaling canary to 40% traffic. continuing to monitor.

emily: do we want to flip fallback routing for the top 5 noisy tenants to smaller model to reduce token pressure?

raj: yes — route top noisy free tenants to compact-embed-v1 for next 30m. That reduces tokens and memory pressure.

sam: executing routing change for top 5 noisy tenants.

sam: routing updated. logs: "routed tenant shoply-ci -> compact-embed-v1" etc.

sam: new telemetry: overall queue depth down 62%, p99 latency down 2.2s, error rate back under 0.2%. premium traffic nominal.

emily: nice work. any follow-ups before we close the pager?

raj: keep the priority_lane flag and lowered timeouts for 1 hour, then reevaluate. plan a rollback path: if we see errors increase for downstream inference, revert routing and restore original max_inflight.

sam: noted. I've created a short-lived runbook entry and an incident note.

support-bot: ACME reply: "Thanks for the update. We'll monitor. Appreciate the proactive routing."

taylor: customer comms done for ACME. No elevated CS tickets so far besides ACME.

emily: recommending post-incident action items: 1) add automated rule to auto-enable priority-lane when queue>80% for 5m 2) evaluate tenant-level token caps 3) revisit default slice max_inflight for low-priority pools.

raj: +1 to all. also add an eval to see if compact-embed-v1 quality is acceptable for the noisy tenants during fallback.

sam: closing loop: promoting canary -> full rollout across us-east. will keep flag on for 1h then start gradual restoration of prior quotas.

emily: thanks team. I'll file a short postmortem and link this thread.

sam: ending on-call here. leaving mitigation in place for 45 more minutes. ping me if regressions. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Pager resolved: queue depth normalized, p99 latency stable. Incident window: 18:43 - 19:15 UTC.
